_comment: Trust policy for the role GitHub Actions assumes to deploy.
NO ACCESS KEYS. The master plan asks for a CI/CD pipeline that halts on a
failed audit; storing a long-lived AWS key pair in repository secrets to
run it would hand an attacker who reads those secrets permanent account
access. GitHub's OIDC provider issues a short-lived token per workflow run
instead, and AWS exchanges it for credentials that expire in an hour.
The permissions this role gets are in github-actions-deploy-policy.json.

_comment_aud: Without this audience check any GitHub Actions run in the WORLD
could assume the role. It is the single most commonly omitted
line in an OIDC trust policy and the most damaging.

_comment_sub: Scoped to this repository and to the branches that are allowed to
deploy. `repo:org/name:*` would let a pull request from a fork run
with deployment credentials, which is a well-known supply-chain
path (OWASP A03) and is exactly what this narrower subject blocks.
